messages.author: 866c5198d7460eae
messages.subject: PGM column in F2 intercross
parts:
Hi all, 

I was wondering if it's possible to combine multiple families in a single input .csv? I have three sets of grandparents that were used to generate four F2 lines e.g./

GP1-F x GP1-M -> F1-1-F x F1-1-M -> F2-1
GP1-F x GP1-M -> F1-2-F x F1-1-M -> F2-2
GP2-F x GP2-M -> F1-3-F x F1-3-M -> F2-3
GP3-F x GP3-M -> F1-4-F x F1-4-M -> F2-4

For the pgm column in the input .csv, is it possible to code the three grandmothers in the 0/1 binary code or can I only load two per file? 

Thank you for your time, 

Sara

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] PGM column in F2 intercross
parts:
No, I think you'd need to keep them separate and then combine them afterwards.

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] PGM column in F2 intercross
parts:
Personally, I'd start by analyzing the families separately, and then either adding LOD scores or just plotting them next to each other.
The joint analysis of multiple crosses with three sets of grandparents is beyond the scope of R/qtl.

karl

messages.author: 04e62c3b36bb17bf
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] PGM column in F2 intercross
parts:
Hi Karl, 
In the past, I ran into something similar. Except just dealing with the first two families:

GP1-F x GP1-M -> F1-1-F x F1-1-M -> F2-1
GP1-F x GP1-M -> F1-2-F x F1-1-M -> F2-2

I made sure that the markers were phased by the two grandparents then concatenated the crosses. 
I then ran scanone with the family identity (F2-1, F2-2) as an additive covariate. 
Was this appropriate?
Thanks,
John

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] PGM column in F2 intercross
parts:
Yes, if you're working with inbred founders. Most of the time there are
multiple sets of F1 parents but they're assumed to be the same.

If you're working with outbred founders, it seems a reasonable starting
point but there is an important assumption about F1-1-F and F1-2-F being
the same.

karl
